items.text: Shift handover, Hearth: I blamed the latch because the paper strip slipped out beside it. After cleaning the channel, the strip grips everywhere except the bottom corner, where the braid has gone shiny and flat. We can replace the gasket after the bun trays come out. Leave the hinge position alone for now. I tucked the groove measurements into H17; check the replacement cold before recording the oven as ready for the next bake.
Margin note beside Q4: battery replaced; zero still wanders.
Downtime board assigns one bench to Hearth's door seal and another to Loft's steam insert. Record both H17 and L22 test results before reopening the ovens.
L22 / Loft oven. Steam jets sideways from the nozzle. Replace the outlet insert; Hearth's gasket order uses the same parts supplier.
Amend Q4 log: final reading was 6 g, not 9 g. A flour streak crossed the handwritten six.
The replacement part arrived in a brown sleeve. I left it beside the service folder; confirm the dimensions before Friday.
Supplier reply on L22: brass insert delayed until Thursday. The steam hose is available, but we did not order a hose.
Trolley C8 wakes the upstairs tenant on the tile seam. Trial rubber casters under the flour rack, retaining its mounting plates.
That measurement was wrong. Use the smaller one on the revised slip, and tell the supplier before dispatch.
Loft steam outlet: revised fitting slot is Friday before breakfast.
C8 wheel trial: soft tread is quiet but catches crumbs. Add a brush to the cleaning kit.
Ticket H17: Hearth's lower door corner leaks heat. Order the woven gasket, measure the groove, and photograph the latch before dismantling.
Post-fit note, L22: mist reaches the rear tray. Retain the removed insert in the fault bag until two test bakes finish.
Use 60 mm wheels for C8; the 75 mm sample catches the shelf bracket. This replaces my earlier size request.
H17 correction in red: the groove is 11 mm, not 14. The first reading included the old seal's swollen lip.
Scale Q4 drifts upward with an empty bowl. Record three empty readings before changing calibration.
Flour rack rolls quietly now. C8 needs one loaded run across the troublesome tile joint before sign-off.
Lower door seal arrived; H17 can move to fitting.
Q4: test weight was dusty. Cleaned it, repeated the series, and still saw the zero climb.
Receiving slip: Hearth gasket H17 and Loft nozzle L22 are in one supplier carton. Count each part against its ticket before closing either repair.
Squash loop W-S now needs six elbows; I forgot the stump detour in the first list.
Pump P2: cup split at the seam; replacement soaked overnight and slides into the bore.
Dawn walk: east beans have a dry middle row. Marked their drip loop E-B with a blue stake; two emitters spit rather than drip.
Far mound reached. W-S is pegged down but awaits its tap.
P2 handle bolt is 8 mm, correcting the 10 mm note pencilled on the shed door.
E-B sketch revision: blocked emitter is at stake six, not five. I counted from the gate, matching the original drawing.
Glasshouse trial G-T: compare coir and leaf-mould mixes in six seedling trays, weighing each before the morning mist.
Water from P2 smells of the soak bucket. Flush the rebuilt shed pump before returning it to use.
Blue stake, E-B: flushed twice; middle row finally damp.
G-T day three: leaf-mould looks drier, yet its tray lost less mass. Appearance alone is misleading.
Barrel sketch: east beans E-B need repaired emitters checked while west squash W-S gets its tap. Mark both outlet positions before drilling.

I returned after the barrel settled because the first flush looked convincing without wetting the root zone. At the east bean loop's blue stake, the middle row was still pale beneath the surface. Removing the second suspect emitter released a clot of grit. I washed both inserts in a bowl, reassembled E-B, and watched a complete slow cycle. Next visit should check that same middle row before burying any exposed tubing. Surface colour alone led us astray on the first visit.
Cross out 240 on tray G-T4; tare label says 204.
Sunday diary: check E-B pressure before filling W-S for its first test, then repeat the bean check with both taps open to measure the squash loop's effect.
West squash layout: peg fresh loop W-S around the mounds. It will draw from the east bean loop's rain barrel through a new outlet tap.
Glasshouse moisture notebook: repeat G-T with the same mist volume, rotating tray positions to counter the door draft.
The watering test still looks wrong. Check the outlet, but first find which bed the unlabelled drawing was meant to show.
W-S shopping scribble: four elbows, one tap, enough tube for the far mound. The donated coil stops a metre short.
Shed pump P2 will not hold prime. Remove the leather cup over a basin so pieces cannot fall into the gravel.
Buy the smaller connector; the drawing in my pocket has yesterday's measurements. I left its heading blank.
V9 sample: narrow tape distorts velvet less than the wide strip. Retain the comparison piece in the archive envelope.
Salt Lantern cutting allocation: finish captain coat SL-C's pleat before trimming the remaining cloth; reserve usable scraps for messenger cape SL-M's hood patch.

Dresser's voice memo: the captain can lift the lantern now, which was the point of opening the back pleat. But watch his storm coat when he turns toward the harbour flat: the loosened fabric catches his belt clasp. Bring SL-C back to the fitting rail and chalk the catch point. Move the clasp loop first, then try the whole turn under the same layered shirt. We should not remove the regained shoulder room just to make the coat look neater on its hanger.
Correction, V9: label reads 'plum', not 'blue'; faded ink fooled me under the lamp.
Rain-costume check: bring SL-C and SL-M under harbour lights. Watch the captain's clasp on the turn and the messenger's hood glare on the run; record each result.
SL-M / messenger cape: shorten the hem above the running boots. Patch its hood with captain storm-coat offcuts so the rain fabrics look related onstage.
Old velvet waistcoat leaves the table once V9's supported seam is photographed flat and on the padded hanger.
The rain fabric catches the light oddly. Bring the garment to the next fitting; this scrap does not say whose costume it is.
For SL-M, use the rough side of the hood patch outward. The shiny side flashes during the messenger's entrance.
Workshop apron batch WA: twelve cotton aprons for the children's backstage session; neck loops must adjust without knots.
I changed the measurement on the card, but the old tape strip is still stuck to the mirror.
Messenger cape SL-M: final hem is 92 cm, replacing the 96 cm on the fitting card.
WA wash test: sample shrank at the pocket. Prewash pocket cloth before cutting the remaining eleven.
Fitting card SL-C: Salt Lantern captain's storm coat pulls when the actor raises the lantern. Release the back pleat before adjusting sleeves.
SL-M waits on the short rail; hood done, hem basted.
WA count amended to fourteen after two workshop helpers joined.
SL-C update: back pleat needs 3 cm release, not the 5 cm pinned at the rushed first fitting.
Archive V9: donated plum velvet waistcoat has powdery seam allowances. Photograph the lining label before adding support tape.
Backstage workshop rail: adjustable aprons ready except two pockets. Mark unfinished pieces WA so helpers do not distribute them.
Captain's storm coat, SL-C: lantern lift now clears comfortably.
Facility card H-R: mount loan-helmet rack beside the desk. Space hooks so straps do not tangle.
The parts tray has the replacement now. I measured it again, but did not copy the job number.
B14 pickup revised to Monday after the commuter's spoke parcel missed collection.
H-R survey found hollow board behind the first bracket position. Move it onto the marked stud.
Job O31: orange delivery bike, rear rim cracked beside a nipple. Rebuild on the replacement rim using the original hub.
Blue commuter B14: fresh spokes seated, final tension pending.
Rack H-R spacing amended from 18 to 22 cm after testing winter helmets.
O31 spoke correction: drive side is 286 mm, not 288. Rechecked flange offset with the hub out.
Green balance bike G6: steering binds at full left lock. Loosen the overtight headset before replacing parts.
Loan helmets remain in cartons; H-R awaits its second bracket.
Orange rear wheel O31: tension even; tyre still off.
G6 turns smoothly after adjustment, but its dust cap rubs. A thin spacer is in the green tray.
Shared spoke order: reserve O31's drive-side set for the orange delivery rebuild and B14's quantities for the blue commuter upgrade. Both use the agreed specification.

Bench card O31: the old rim looked straight until unloaded, when the crack opened enough to catch a fingernail. The orange delivery bike's hub bearings feel smooth, so the rebuild still uses that hub. I laced the new rim and brought the spokes up gradually, but stopped before final stress relief because one replacement nipple was rough. Swap that nipple, check lateral runout again, then fit the tyre and try the wheel with delivery bags loaded. A bare-wheel spin will not reveal how it behaves on the usual rounds.
G6 correction: spacer is 2 mm; the 3 mm sample leaves insufficient thread engagement.
Wheel afternoon: finish orange delivery O31's stress test, then use its tension record as the reference for bringing blue commuter B14 up to target.
Job B14: blue commuter needs a stronger rear wheel. Copy orange delivery job O31's spoke specification while retaining the commuter's existing rim.
Green balance bike ready for floor check. Sign G6 after the fork falls freely both ways.
Rear wheel is ready except for final tension. The bike is by the stand; I forgot to replace its job tag.
B14 parts slip: commuter spokes sorted; existing rim cleaned and passed eyelet inspection.
BX ready for a packed-box shake after its tab glue dries.
A / core freight: five-coin start produced two contested auctions.
LP table quote: 'I thought my basket could spoil safely because hers was full.' Put the shared spoil counter beside the weather deck.
Economy review: run Glass Harbour auction A with five coins, then add tugboat expansion T without replenishing cash. Record freight bids and tow purchases on the session sheet.

Glass Harbour session A transcript: 'Buying the first crate felt like losing because then I had nothing for the dock fee.' We replayed the freight order with the larger starting purse and got more bidding without changing the fee. I cannot tell whether the last player still has a disadvantage; an experienced bidder occupied that seat in the second run. Keep the next freight deck order fixed, rotate seats, and record unspent coins each round. That should isolate the starting cash change before we rewrite the auction itself.
LP amendment: loss threshold is four spoiled baskets for the small deck; three remains the large-deck trial.
T's permit price waits on A's starting-purse decision. Bring the auction ledger and tugboat draft to Thursday's review, including unspent-coin totals from each.
Tugboat expansion T: buy tow permits after Glass Harbour's freight auction. Reuse the core coin supply rather than introducing another currency.
Last Pear: weather-deck reminder worked. LP players explained the common loss before their second turn.
The next table should try a different limit. I wrote down both three and four, but forgot which rule we were discussing.
T session: players hoard tow permits because the rescue bonus looks generous. Pay only when a stalled vessel actually moves.
Carry-box insert BX: folded walls collapse beneath wooden tokens. Prototype a double fold along the long compartment.
The latest rule needs a clearer example. Bring the marked cards, whichever packet we used at the last table.
T erratum: a tug tows one vessel per round, not two. The example diagram already shows the intended limit.
BX drop check: double fold survives, but the small divider pops out. Add a locking tab.
Glass Harbour core, auction log A: opening bids leave no coins for shipping. Test a four-coin starting purse with freight cards unchanged.
Tugboat T prototype: replace rescue-bonus text on six permit cards.
BX width corrected to 214 mm internal; 224 included the outer cardboard shell.
Ledger A correction: starting purse should be five coins; four was the control, copied into the proposal by mistake.
Last Pear LP: cooperative orchard game needs a clearer shared-loss condition. Trial ending when three baskets spoil.
The quiet room still needs a sign. Leave it outside so visitors can read it before entering.
NR prep chat: fireplace guard fitted; move the covered bed because the upstairs radiator clicks against its frame.
Bedding cupboard BC: mend the blue fleece stack and count usable washable pads before ordering replacements.
The supplies are packed, but the revised count is on another slip. Confirm it before leaving.
Nori NR revision: smaller bed fits the alcove; the large one on the first list blocks the outlet.
BC repair note: two fleeces have torn binding and sound centres. Rebind those; put the fraying pad in the rag bag.
Bramble room card BR: block the gap behind the low cabinet. Place the covered bed where opening the door will not expose it.
NR upstairs sign printed; the alcove bed still needs unpacking.
BC total amended from eighteen to sixteen usable pads; two appeared on both folded and wash lists.
BR correction: water bowl belongs on the window wall, not beside the bed; the first sketch leaves too little walking space.
Rabbit transport RT: book the estate car for Saturday's move of Pip and Thistle to their weekend foster home. Both carriers must sit level.
Supply cupboard BC: blue fleece binding finished; pad order awaits the corrected inventory count.
Bramble's cabinet gap is blocked. BR still needs its sign.
RT driver note: boot slopes, so place carriers on the flat rear seat with the approved cupboard restraints.
Room visit: finish Bramble BR's door-screen check downstairs, then test Nori NR's fireplace guard upstairs. Bring two adapted checklists and mark the room name on each.

Handover chat, Bramble BR: I sat on the floor to see what arrival would look like. From bed height the open door points straight at the basket, although the overhead sketch looked sheltered. I turned the covered bed toward the cabinet and kept a clear path to the water on the window wall. The cabinet gap is blocked now. Check that the cardboard screen stays upright when the door swings, then put the quiet-room sign outside. Those are the last preparation jobs before Bramble arrives.
RT pickup now 09:30, replacing 08:45 after the weekend home changed its handover slot.
Delivery covers BR's door screen and NR's smaller bed. Put Bramble's item downstairs and Nori's upstairs, then update both room-readiness cards.
Nori room NR: adapt Bramble BR's checklist for the upstairs spare room. No cabinet here, but the open fireplace needs a fitted guard.
Pip and Thistle's RT carrier labels sit beside the car booking.
Loft measurement correction: opening width is 81 cm; the earlier 84 included the trim. I have crossed it out on the north-window sketch.
Cylinder cupboard note: fit a jacket around the hot-water cylinder after measuring the accessible gap, without covering its controls or vent.
Bedroom rug corners lie flat over the new grippy underlay.
North loft sash: paper-strip test now grips along the hinge edge.
Cupboard sketch: the cylinder's left clearance is tighter than its right. Choose the jacket with separate fastening straps.
Quote review: north loft work needs sash seals plus hinge labour; study work needs a removable inner pane. Ask the shared supplier to show those two totals before approving the window visit.

Email to the installer, draft saved: I spent last evening checking the north loft window with the curtain drawn back. The cold line follows the opening sash and is strongest beside the upper hinge. The central pane feels cool too, but that is not where the moving air comes through. Please price the compressible seal and hinge adjustment we discussed, using the corrected opening measurement on the sketch. I can clear the loft desk on Tuesday. After fitting, I want to repeat the paper-strip check at the same four points before replacing the curtain.
Cylinder jacket correction: height available is 103 cm, not 113; a shelf support interrupts the top space.
Installer access email: clear the loft desk for the north sash repair and move the study chair for inner-panel measuring. Both window appointments use Tuesday's lift booking.
Subject: study glazing quote. Add a removable inner panel for the study window to the north loft repair supplier's quote. Study condensation is the concern here.
Hot-water cupboard jacket delivered. Check the control opening against the cylinder before fastening its straps.
The window measurements need checking before the supplier cuts the new piece. The room name has torn off this slip.
Study panel email: supplier proposes magnetic edging so we can remove the inner pane to clean the trapped space.
Bedroom rug trial: add dense acoustic underlay to soften footfall heard downstairs. Start with the rectangle beside the bed.
The sample fits at one end but not the other. Compare it with the revised sketch before ordering the full size.
Revision to study order: clear panel, not the frosted finish listed in the first quotation; the reading desk needs the light.
Underlay sample beneath the bedroom rug is quiet but slides. Ask for a grippy backing before ordering the full piece.
Subject: north loft window. Cold air comes around the opening sash, not through the glass. Ask for compressible seals and a hinge adjustment.
Study glazing: magnetic sample sticks firmly; full pane uncut.
Bedroom underlay size amended to 180 by 240; the first measurement included rug fringe.
Celadon trial, run Willow: borrow the cooling segment from amber run Aster, then compare pale-green tiles with and without the short intermediate soak.
Kiln post tray: four new short supports sit flat and are marked.
The test tiles came out uneven. Repeat a pair in different positions, using the same settings once we recover their glaze labels.
Willow cone packet: pale-green tile beside the door came out cloudier. Add a tile at the rear for the next celadon comparison.
Reclaim corner: make slatted drying boards for the studio's wet clay, sized to fit over the sink without blocking the tap.
A number on this firing slip was copied incorrectly. The run name is missing, so match it to the notebook before filing.
Willow label amendment: rear tile is C7, not C1. The tiny crossbar disappeared beneath kiln wash.
Reclaim board trial: narrow slats sag beneath wet clay. Add a central crosspiece to the sink-sized prototype.
Firing book, amber cups / run Aster: pinholes cluster on shoulders. Keep the glaze recipe fixed and trial a longer hold at peak.
Celadon Willow: rear comparison tile glazed; firing slot pending.
Drying-board sketch correction: sink span is 58 cm, not 68. Measured between ledges this time.
Aster correction: peak hold was twelve minutes, not twenty; the controller photo resolves my smudged notebook entry.
Shelf-support inspection: three short posts in the community kiln have chipped rims. Mark them with chalk and measure replacements while cold.
Reclaim corner boards sanded; waiting for the crosspiece glue to cure before loading wet clay.
Amber Aster shoulder tiles: fewer pinholes after the longer hold.
Post tray note: replacement short supports rock on the flat board. One base needs inspection before it goes into the kiln.
Schedule notebook: copy Aster's amber cooling segment into Willow's celadon draft, then annotate the proposed Willow soak beside the unchanged Aster values for the firing review.

Aster unloading observation: the top shelf cups show the pinholes most clearly, especially where the amber glaze crosses the rounded shoulder. Flat test tiles made the first run look better than it was. For the next firing I want both tiles and two matching cups on each shelf, with the same glaze thickness recorded before loading. Keep the longer peak hold, but avoid changing the cooling segment yet. If the pinholes differ by shelf again, photograph the witnesses alongside the pots before anyone carries the amber batch to the sales table.
Support count corrected to four chipped short posts; one had been hiding under the kiln shelf cart.
Kiln meeting tray: bring Aster's amber shoulder cups and Willow's pale-green tiles. We need both sets beside their witnesses before deciding whether the shared cooling segment is worth retaining.
Birch lower-junction panel painted; upper-junction blank still drying.
Boot-brush order revised to two heads; one is too narrow for the broad boots used in the trial.
Alder paint list correction: four panels need replacement, not three; the return arrow beyond bend 4 was missed on the first walk.
Moss path bridge: eastern handrail wobbles where the lower bolt enters its post. Inspect that joint before planning a full rail replacement.
Trailhead cleaning frame anchored; brush heads will fit after the paint cures.
Alder bend 4: new arrow readable from both approaches.
Moss bridge inspection found a sound rail and enlarged bolt hole. Fit the agreed repair plate at the eastern post.
Paint day: cut Alder's four replacement panels and Birch's two new junction panels from the shared sheet. Print the common arrow artwork once, then add each route's lettering.

Volunteer walk notes: from the uphill approach, the Alder loop arrow at bend 4 is visible well before the fork. From below, the tall grass hides its lower half until walkers are almost level with it. The new lettering has enough contrast; moving the post would mean drilling new holes into a sound base. Trim the small patch of grass first and repeat the walk with someone who has not memorized the route. Check the other three replacement panels on the same round, and take photographs from a walker's eye height rather than directly in front of each sign.
Moss handrail hardware correction: plate needs four holes, not two, matching the approved sketch.
Route review walk covers Alder bend 4's sight line and Birch's lower-junction distance label. Carry both sign lists so the shared arrow style can be checked in place.
Birch spur survey: add arrows at its two new junctions. Reuse the Alder loop arrow artwork, with Birch's destination names and distances.
Eastern handrail on Moss bridge holds firm; photograph the repaired joint.
The new arrow panel needs a visibility check from both directions. Someone removed the route name from this paint-day slip.
Birch layout note: the long 'Quarry View' destination wraps awkwardly; widen the new spur panel rather than shrinking every letter.
Trailhead boot station: trial a fixed brush beside the gravel apron so mud stays outside the information shelter.
We need the revised count before collecting the painted pieces. The first list is in someone's bag.
Birch distance correction: Quarry View is 0.8 km from the lower junction; 1.1 was measured from the gate.
Boot-station mockup catches long laces on its bracket. Round the bracket edge and retest with walking boots.
Alder loop survey, bend 4: direction arrow has faded to a white patch. Replace the three sun-facing signs using the old mounting holes.
Pebble correction: evening feed was at 19:00, not 21:00; the kitchen timer photo has the right time.
Label audit before tasting: verify Ruby B's corrected fill weight and Sun's triangle-marked dill jar. These are the two entries that changed on the shared fermentation diary page.
Sun / carrot sticks: use Ruby's cabbage tasting dates as the diary schedule. Test one jar with dill and one plain, marking the lid shapes as well as colours.
Rye starter Pebble rose past the band before breakfast again.
The jar with the darker lid tastes sharper today. I cannot find the page that says what its mark means.
Sun tasting slip: plain carrot jar has the cleaner aroma; dill jar still has a firmer bite. Keep these as observations, not a final winner.
Shelf plan: shade the fermentation jars from the bright kitchen window with a ventilated backboard and a shallow retaining lip.
Retake the jar photographs in even light before writing the tasting comparison. Match the pictures to the labels first.
Sun label revision: dill jar has the triangular lid mark; I reversed triangle and circle in yesterday's diary.
Shaded-shelf mockup: retaining lip hides the lowest jar labels. Lower the lip before cutting the final board.
Ruby / red cabbage: compare the two labelled salt levels using equal jar fill weights. Photograph each surface before the first tasting day.
Sun carrot photographs retaken; triangular lid mark is now visible.
Shelf depth corrected to 24 cm; the 28 cm sketch would obstruct the window handle.
Ruby label correction: jar B holds 420 g of cabbage, not 470; the latter included the empty jar lid.
Pebble rye starter: track rise marks after evening feeds for a week; the latest feed peaked while I was asleep.
Kitchen jar shelf sanded; the ventilated backboard still needs fixing.
Ruby day six: both cabbage jars still crisp; B tangier.
Pebble jar note: lower starting line made the overnight rise easier to read. Keep the elastic band at that line.
Tasting calendar: Ruby cabbage and Sun carrots share Sunday and Wednesday diary slots. Lay out fresh spoons for both experiments and enter each jar's observations on its own line.

Tasting diary, Ruby: I expected the two cabbage jars to differ mainly in crunch, but today the sharper difference was how long the sour taste lingered. I tasted from plain spoons and wrote the first impression before looking at which salt label belonged to which jar. Both still have a crisp bite. Leave the fill weights and the next tasting day as planned; changing the schedule halfway through would make my earlier notes less useful. I also need to photograph the surface in consistent light, because yesterday's warm lamp made jar B appear a different colour.
Folder shelf trial: thicker board fits, but the central support obscures one label holder. Move that holder to the front lip.
Winter Window opening set: altos enter late after bar 18. Rehearse the shared breath through the rest before returning to full tempo.
Lantern Walk arc worked; the last row saw every entrance.
Choir shelf span corrected to 76 cm; 79 measured the outside of the side panels.
Opening-set pencil correction: difficult entry is bar 19, not 18; the pickup belongs to the preceding measure in this edition.
Archive pronunciation project: record spoken guide tracks for the Meadow Book songs, one verse per file with an audible verse number.
Music folders can return when the replacement lower shelf's finish dries.
Winter Window altos: shared breath fixed the late entry today.
Meadow Book recording note: verse three's final consonant clipped. Retake the spoken line with more silence before stopping.
Warm-up plan: lead Winter Window's shared-breath drill, check its alto entry, then repeat the exercise with Lantern Walk's street-corner cues. Mark separate results for the concert and outdoor sets.

Conductor transcript, Winter Window opener: the altos have the notes, so another slow note-learning pass will not solve what we heard. They watch the page through the rest and miss the preparation for their entry. Ask everyone to look up on the shared breath, sing just the landing chord, then restore the preceding phrase. When we put the whole opening set back together, record the entry once from the back of the room. The piano beside the singers masks the delay more than it does for someone sitting where the audience will be.
Meadow Book file correction: track labelled verse five is verse four; the spoken number at its start is accurate.
Choir committee note: Winter Window's opening-set rehearsal and Lantern Walk's arc trial both need the main room Thursday. Divide the booking so each group gets its planned run-through.
Lantern Walk outdoor set: reuse Winter Window's shared-breath exercise, then practice the street-corner entrances without piano support.
Spoken Meadow Book guides exported; check the verse labels once more.
The entrance is late again after the silent beat. Try watching the leader instead of the page.
Lantern Walk run-through: the corner cue disappears when singers stand in one long line. Trial a shallow arc around the leader.
Choir-room shelves: replace the sagging lower boards that hold music folders. Measure with the folders removed so the bow does not distort the span.
The set needs another run-through with the corrected cues. This photocopy is missing its heading; recover that before putting it on the rehearsal stand.
Lantern Walk order revised: place the short round second, ahead of the long refrain, to suit the walk between stops.
Media-transfer day: log the display canister's flow before removing the pouch, then log the shrimp nursery's circulation after fitting it. Attach both readings to the transfer record.

Weekend care log: the display tank's outlet stream is back at the tape mark after cleaning the intake sponge. I nearly opened the whole canister, but checked the visible intake first and found the obstruction there. Record another bucket-fill comparison before touching the internal baskets. If the flow falls again, note whether loose plant fragments are collecting on the sponge after trimming. The cabinet card still carries the corrected fill time, so copy that value rather than the wet notebook page with the reversed digits.
Spare aquarium label amended: the marked panel is the back, not the base; rotate the sketch accordingly.
Weekend check sheet pairs display intake inspection with nursery pouch inspection. Note any flow change in the display and whether the nursery's gentle elbow remains correctly seated.
Shrimp nursery setup: seed its small filter with a measured pouch of media from the planted display canister. Record the transfer on the nursery card.
Empty spare's mineral line gone; rinse and inspect the corners.
The outlet is weaker today. Check the filter before changing the layout; I forgot which tank this reading came from.
Nursery card: pouch is in the small filter and the bare tank is circulating. Keep logging observations before introducing any shrimp.
Supply cabinet build: fit a raised plinth and washable door fronts so splashes do not soak the aquarium food and spare tools.
The corrected number belongs on a fresh tank card. Find the card heading before copying it; the quantity has no units on this scrap.
Nursery equipment correction: use the gentle outlet elbow, not the spray bar shown in the first layout.
Cabinet mockup: food tubs fit above the plinth, but long tongs hit the door. Add a shallow side hook.
Display tank flow card: canister output has fallen since the intake sponge clogged. Clean the sponge and mark the outlet stream position for comparison.
Shrimp nursery circulation gentle now; transfer pouch remains in place.
Supply cabinet width corrected to 42 cm; the first drawing ignored the wall pipe.
Display flow log correction: bucket fill took 48 seconds, not 84; transposed the digits while drying my hands.
Empty spare aquarium: remove the white mineral line before storing it. Test the cleaning pad on an inconspicuous patch of glass first.
Washable cabinet doors fitted; side hook for the tongs still loose.
Display canister: cleaned sponge restored the stream to its mark.
Spare-glass trial: soft pad removes the mineral haze without visible scratches under side lighting. Continue a small section at a time.
The drawing has the old number. Bring the revised sheet before we cut any more pieces.
Birch attachment correction: tray width is 16 cm, not 18; the larger cutout catches the wheel guard.
Maze table trial: visitors confuse the goal square with an obstacle. Add a flag symbol to the paper grid's goal.
Bug LF-8, Cedar: robot overshoots the black line on tight bends. Log left and right sensor readings while rolling the chassis slowly through the corner.
Birch parcel tray clears both wheels; retaining edge still untested.
Paper maze correction: print a six-by-six grid, not seven-by-seven; the arrow cards fit the smaller layout better.
LF-8 correction: the low threshold is 320, not 230. We swapped the numbers while copying the serial log.
Battery inventory BI: count rechargeable packs in the robotics cupboard and label their connector types before the club's next loan session.
Open-day arrow-card maze printed; reset instruction now visible at the start.
Cedar LF-8: slow corner pass now stays over the line.
BI cupboard check found two packs without legible connector labels. Set them aside from the loan-ready stock pending identification.
Fabrication note: measure Cedar's revised sensor bracket after LF-8's slow pass, then transfer that hole pattern to Birch's parcel-tray drawing before cutting its mount.

Student notebook, Cedar LF-8: we thought the steering code was late because the robot kept drifting wide at the painted corner. Pushing the chassis by hand showed that the right sensor stopped seeing the line before the left one reached it. We moved the sensor bracket slightly forward and repeated the slow pass with the motors disabled. The readings look less abrupt now. Save that log alongside the corrected threshold, then run the powered trial at the previous speed. Changing speed and bracket position together would leave us unsure which adjustment helped.
BI count revised from twelve to ten loan-ready packs; the two unlabeled ones were included in the first total.
Club demo schedule: run Cedar's line-following corner check, then Birch's loaded delivery turn on the same cleared floor. Capture the sensor fix and tray test as separate notebook entries.
Birch delivery attachment: copy Cedar's sensor-mount hole pattern for the parcel tray bracket. The tray must clear Birch's front wheels when loaded.
Robotics cupboard BI sheet updated; connector labels await a final check.
It veers during the turn again. Check the bracket position before adjusting anything; the robot name is missing from this trial sheet.
Birch tray issue: parcel shifts on the turn and tips the bracket. Add a low retaining edge before repeating the loaded run.
Open-day maze draft: a paper grid for visitors to guide a pretend robot using arrow cards. Leave space for a reset instruction near the start.
Maple centre opens up now; coarse stems still visible.
Bucket rota note: west-door label faded in the rain. Replace it with a covered label showing the same pickup day.
